<awtsmoosMeluketTranslation heichel="ikar" alias="meluket_translation_en" seriesId="חשון_meluket" postId="BH_POST_1766518914855_theRebbe_522" batchId="meluket-_D7_97_D7_A9_D7_95_D7_9F_meluket__BH_POST_1766518914855_theRebbe_522__p001">
  <section v="0">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section provides the opening header and date for the maamar.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">With the help of Heaven.</t>
    <t s="1">On the eve of Monday, Parshat Chayei Sarah,</t>
    <t s="2">the 20th of MarCheshvan, 5746</t>
  </section>
  <section v="1">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains the allegory of the woman crying to Elisha, identifying the soul as the woman, her husband as the lost love of G-d, the creditor as the animal soul, and the flask of oil as the essence of the soul.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">"And a certain woman of the wives of the sons of the prophets cried out to Elisha, etc."</t>
    <t s="1">It is known from the discourse of the Alter Rebbe on the verse,</t>
    <t s="2">that "woman" refers to the soul,</t>
    <t s="3">and it is called "one woman" because it is one with Havayah,</t>
    <t s="4">"of the wives of the sons of the prophets,"</t>
    <t s="5">for "prophets" is from the term "utterance of the lips,"</t>
    <t s="6">meaning they receive from the aspect of "the word of Havayah," and the soul is a vessel to receive perceptions and revelations of G-dliness.</t>
    <t s="7">And "Elisha" is the letters of "Eli Sha," which is the Holy One, blessed be He.</t>
    <t s="8">And this is: "And a certain woman... cried out to Elisha,"</t>
    <t s="9">that the soul cries out to the Holy One, blessed be He,</t>
    <t s="10">"Your servant, my husband, is dead."</t>
    <t s="11">"My husband" is "Eish" (fire) and Yud,</t>
    <t s="12">for the love that was like "flames of fire" that I had, to be included and nullified in the aspect of the Yud of Supernal Chochmah—is dead,</t>
    <t s="13">meaning that now I do not have this love.</t>
    <t s="14">"And the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves."</t>
    <t s="15">"And the creditor," from the term "for G-d has made me forget,"</t>
    <t s="16">refers to the animal soul, which causes me to forget G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="17">and "my two children" are love and fear.</t>
    <t s="18">[As explained in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="19">that the emotions are called "offspring,"</t>
    <t s="20">and the primary emotions are love and fear],</t>
    <t s="21">and this is: "And the creditor has come to take my two children for himself as slaves,"</t>
    <t s="22">to [become] foreign loves and foreign fears.</t>
    <t s="23">[For in addition to the animal soul causing me to forget G-dliness and wanting, G-d forbid, to nullify the love and fear of G-dliness,</t>
    <t s="24">it wants to take the love and fear of the G-dly soul to be slaves to the animal soul].</t>
    <t s="25">"And Elisha said to her, 'What do you have in the house?'"</t>
    <t s="26">What powers remain with you over which the animal soul has no control?</t>
    <t s="27">"And she said, 'Your maidservant has nothing... except a flask of oil.'"</t>
    <t s="28">That nothing remained with her except the essential point of the soul.</t>
    <t s="29">[It can be said,</t>
    <t s="30">that "oil" is Chochmah,</t>
    <t s="31">and "a flask of oil" is the aspect of Chochmah within the soul,</t>
    <t s="32">over which the animal soul has no control].</t>
    <t s="33">"And he said, 'Go, borrow vessels for yourself from outside... empty vessels, do not make few.'"</t>
    <t s="34">That you should engage in Torah and mitzvos,</t>
    <t s="35">which are vessels for the light of Havayah,</t>
    <t s="36">and even though the Torah and mitzvos you are now engaged in are empty vessels</t>
    <t s="37">(without love and fear),</t>
    <t s="38">nevertheless, "do not make few" of them,</t>
    <t s="39">"and you shall pour [oil] upon all these vessels,"</t>
    <t s="40">to draw into them the revelation of the essence of the soul.</t>
    <t s="41">[In the manner explained in Tanya,</t>
    <t s="42">that the fulfillment of the Torah and its mitzvos depends on this, that one always remember the matter of self-sacrifice to G-d,</t>
    <t s="43">for self-sacrifice is from the aspect of the essence of the soul].</t>
    <t s="44">"And when you do this, then you and your sons shall live on the remainder,"</t>
    <t s="45">like the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness.</t>
    <t s="46">And there is another interpretation of "empty vessels, do not make few,"</t>
    <t s="47">that one should contemplate greatly</t>
    <t s="48">how he is an empty vessel, without knowledge in the brain and without awe and love,</t>
    <t s="49">and he should become very bitter over his distance,</t>
    <t s="50">and through this, the light of the soul will shine within him.</t>
    <t s="51">And as the saying of the Head of the Academy in the Garden of Eden:</t>
    <t s="52">"Wood in which no light shines, they strike it... a body in which the light of the soul does not shine, they strike it and light shines in it."</t>
    <t s="53">And moreover, this light</t>
    <t s="54">(that shines through the bitterness of being an empty vessel)</t>
    <t s="55">has an advantage over the light as it is in itself,</t>
    <t s="56">specifically like the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness.</t>
    <t s="57">And this is: "And you and your sons shall live on the remainder,"</t>
    <t s="58">"you" is the essence of the soul, and "your sons" are the awe and love within each soul—"shall live on the remainder,"</t>
    <t s="59">like the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness.</t>
  </section>
  <section v="2">
    <sectionSummaryBrief>This section explains that the advantage of light from darkness achieved through bitter contemplation of being empty is superior to that achieved through performing mitzvos without love and fear.</sectionSummaryBrief>
    <t s="0">2)</t>
    <t s="1">It can be said,</t>
    <t s="2">that the advantage of the light that comes from the darkness</t>
    <t s="3">("and you and your sons shall live on the remainder")</t>
    <t s="4">according to the interpretation of "empty vessels, do not make few" that one should contemplate greatly how he is an empty vessel,</t>
    <t s="5">is more elevated than the advantage of the light</t>
    <t s="6">("remainder")</t>
    <t s="7">according to the interpretation of "empty vessels, do not make few" that one should engage in Torah and mitzvos even though they are without love and fear.</t>
    <t s="8">For behold, regarding the advantage of light from darkness,</t>
    <t s="9">there are two matters.</t>
    <t s="10">[First,] the advantage of the light in order to illuminate the darkness.</t>
    <t s="11">That in order to illuminate a very distant and dark place,</t>
    <t s="12">a very great light is needed.</t>
    <t s="13">For so it is also regarding the advantage</t>
    <t s="14">("shall live on the remainder")</t>
    <t s="15">that comes through engaging in Torah and mitzvos without love and fear,</t>
    <t s="16">for this—that he engages in Torah and mitzvos even though he has no love and fear—</t>
    <t s="17">is because of the intensity of his connection to G-dliness from the aspect of the essence of the soul,</t>
    <t s="18">which is above the revealed faculties.</t>
    <t s="19">And there is another matter regarding the advantage of light from darkness,</t>
    <t s="20">that through the bitterness over the darkness that conceals His infinite light,</t>
    <t s="21">there is drawn forth from the aspect of "He made darkness His hiding place,"</t>
    <t s="22">a darkness that is above light</t>
    <t s="23">(above even a great light that illuminates even in the darkest place).</t>
    <t s="24">And this is the advantage</t>
    <t s="25">("shall live on the remainder")</t>
    <t s="26">that comes through contemplating how he is an empty vessel,</t>
    <t s="27">for through the bitterness over being an empty vessel</t>
    <t s="28">(darkness),</t>
    <t s="29">he reaches the aspect of darkness that is above light.</t>
  </section>
</awtsmoosMeluketTranslation>
